candidates.lead: Don Toliver fans say they were asked to strip and held for hours after an evacuation at Co-op Live
candidates.evidence_text: Don Toliver Co-op Live evacuation quarantine traumatic, fans say - BBC News Image source, Handout Image caption, Jordan said they were taken to a sports court on the Etihad campus and were told they would not be able to leave By Georgie Docker and Kelly Foran , North West Published 26 November 2026 Some Don Toliver fans who were evacuated from Manchester's Co-op Live arena after an unknown substance was released have said they were "quarantined for six hours" and threatened with arrest if they did not remove all their clothing. Jordan, 33, from Scotland, said he and his brothers were among 88 people who were taken for decontamination after the incident at the gig on Sunday night , and it "felt like I was being taken hostage". He said they had asked for medical help at 22:15 GMT and were taken to the Etihad Stadium, where they were made to change into paper suits, and stayed until 04:45 on Monday. "It was so traumatic," Jordan said. Greater Manchester Police declined to comment. The force has not confirmed what the substance was and there have been no arrests. A woman was taken to hospital, with 88 other people reporting symptoms, including coughing and chest pains. Dry decontamination was carried out by North West Ambulance Service (NWAS), GMP said. NWAS said it had deployed crews, including its Hazardous Area Response Team, who carried out decontamination "as a precaution" in line with "advice taken from national scientific advisors based on the situation". Image source, Handout Image caption, Concertgoers said they were held for hours and asked to strip after an evacuation at Co-op Live Jordan said his 15-year-old brother first approached police officers for help when they all started to develop symptoms 15 minutes after the incident. "Our eyes started to feel like one sensation and then we started to feel like chest pains and coughs," he said. "We went there for help, they obviously knew that they were keeping people there, but they never told us, 'once you're in you can't get out'. Three hours later - at about 01:30 on Monday - Jordan said the fire service told concertgoers that they would have to remove their clothes before being taken in a van to another area of Etihad Campus. According to NHS England guidance , external , dry decontamination - the use of a dry material to remove a contaminant - should be the "default intervention" for anyone suspected of being contaminated in a chemical incident. The guidance also suggests patients should "remove outer clothing if affected by the substance". Image source, Handout Image caption, Jordan said he was initially told he would not have his clothes returned for two weeks "They said we had to strip down, clothes off, put paper overalls on and then we had to get moved into a quarantine area which was across the road," Jordan said. Jordan claimed when he expressed concern to police officers, who were also based inside the sports hall, and asked why they needed to remove their clothes he was threatened with arrest. "They said if I didn't commit to the decontamination, I would be arrested and charged for breach of the peace," he said. Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service have also been approached for comment. Image source, Handout Image caption, About 70 quarantined concertgoers were allegedly held for more than six hours before being released In a previous statement, GMFRS said crews had been in attendance for about seven hours "to ensure the safety of every person attending the event". GMP said 88 people were "accommodated within the Etihad Stadium while the incident was managed". Jordan said that at about 04:45 an officer told them that if they gave their details they would be able to go. Image caption, Archie Grime, from Accrington, said he was sitting "doing nothing for hours" during the quarantine "We received our clothes and shoes, but we were not allowed to put them back on, he said. "We had to walk back to the hotel in socks and the paper gown in the freezing cold." Jordan said he and his two brothers were both receiving further medical treatment after being advised to attend hospital in Scotland. A group of friends from Scunthorpe, Molly, 19, Kyan 22, Charlie, 20, and Jack, 21, said they were also "up all night" during the decontamination process. They said it was "confusing" and there was not much information about what was happening and why. candidates.lead: John Morris believes the loss of his son was due to radiation exposure picked up on Christmas Island
candidates.evidence_text: Nuclear veteran says investigation a 'magical moment' - BBC News Image caption, John Morris has long campaigned for a study into the health impacts of Britain's nuclear programme By Richard Baker North West Published 26 November 2026 A nuclear test veteran who developed cancer and lost his four-month-old son, has said hearing an independent panel will look into Britain's atomic programme was "a magical moment". John Morris, from Rochdale, was sent to Christmas Island in the 1950s to work on the UK's growing nuclear programme - and now believes the loss of his son was due to radiation exposure picked up on the island. It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced an investigation into the lasting health impacts of testing exercises in the 1950s and 60s. Morris, who alongside fellow veterans have long campaigned for an investigation, said this announcement feels different "without a shadow of a doubt". "He [Burnham] has delivered something that has taken more than 70 years to come to fruition, I can't thank you enough," Morris told BBC North West Tonight . Image caption, Burnham told campaigners in Downing Street that he would launch an independent investigation Morris said he was 18 when he was sent to Christmas Island, in the Pacific Ocean, to work as a laundry operator on a British nuclear site. The island was a major Anglo American nuclear site in the Cold War period, lying just north of Australia. "I thought we were helping soldiers build a runway, I have no idea why, and suddenly we found out we were testing atomic bombs," Morris said. He said safety concerns when a blast went off were relaxed, with him being told to turn his back to the explosion and cover his eyes. "If I asked you to sit 20 miles from the centre of the sun with a pair of trousers and a shutter, I think you'd have certain words to say. "I was ordered to sit 20 miles from a megaton explosion. The heat, the power, the smell was frightening," he added. Despite these experiences being nearly 70 years ago, the 2023 release of multi-award winning Oppenheimer, which charted America's own post-war nuclear programme, brought it all back for Morris. "I couldn't get off my seat, I was transported to being 18 again," he said. Image caption, Morris was 18 when he worked as a laundry operator at a nuclear site Many of the surviving veterans said they were more likely to develop a range of illnesses in the years that followed, while their descendants said they had suffered an increased risk of hereditary illnesses and fertility problems. "I lost a son at four months old, I was told it was bronchial pneumonia - it turned out that his lungs hadn't formed properly. "It took me 50 years under the Freedom of Information act to get his autopsy, now that's not normal," he said. Morris has just welcomed three grandchildren, but recounts being "terrified" that they would have been born with an extra limb or deformed. The announcement of an independent panel is the culmination of years of campaigning by the Labrats (Legacy of the Atomic Bomb: Recognition for Atomic Test Survivors) group and others, and comes 14 years after a legal challenge at the UK Supreme Court failed. Speaking of his fellow campaigners, Morris said: "Not only have we had cancer, we've had heart disease, men infertile because their sperm's been altered, we've had children born with deficiencies." The independent panel will be modelled on the Hillsborough Independent Panel and chaired by the same person, James Jones, the former Bishop of Liverpool. Downing Street said it would produce a report by October 2027 to coincide with the 75th anniversary of the first British nuclear weapons test. candidates.lead: Jacqui Carroll wanted to help other working class people gain experience in the industry
candidates.evidence_text: The film company in Manchester that started with £50 and a camera - BBC News Image caption, Jacqui Carroll wanted to give aspiring film makers new opportunities By Kelly Foran North West Published 26 November 2026 In 2001, Jacqui Carroll and Terry Egan started a film and documentary company from their home with just £50, a digital video camera and a belief that everyone has a story worth telling. Now, a quarter of a century later, the stories captured on film will form part of the North West Film Archive. REELMCR was set up to help other working class people gain opportunities and experience in an industry that Jacqui said always felt like it was for a "different class". "When I was in school I said I wanted to be an actor or an astronaut and was laughed at," she said. "I was told I could be a receptionist and that's what I ended up doing. "When I was 39 and pregnant with my daughter I had to stay in and watch TV. "That's when I realised there was nobody who sounded like me and people I knew on TV. "Even in the soaps they were putting the accents on." Image caption, Terry Egan said he felt the biggest amount of pride when the people involved watched their work Jacqui and Terry decided to set up the company in Manchester making films and documentaries as well as providing training and projects in working-class communities. From the sound engineers to the scriptwriters, everyone involved was given a chance to shine. "I was a reader and got my education in other ways," said Terry, who admits he did not attend school. "But ReelMCR... it would have been just what I needed when I was growing up. "It would have made my life easier." Image source, REELMCR Image caption, Our Sam (The Middleton Man) featuring Tom Charnock was produced by REELMCR Over the past 25 years, the production company has also been a hub of the region's creative talent. "It was life changing," said independent script supervisor Jodie Woodall, who directed Bafta-nominated programme At Home with the Rirchardsons, about her time with REELMCR. "Their knowledge, enthusiasm and passion gave me the courage to go on to pursue a career in film – something I never thought possible before meeting the REELMCR team." Early films including Theatre of Dream, which was made in Hulme in 2001, and Urban Culture, which was filmed in Gorton, began a growing body of work rooted in local lives. Now the stories and memories that have been captured on film are about to take on a new life after REELMCR secured a grant from The National Lottery Heritage Fund to safeguard its extensive archive. The 12-month heritage programme will see the company recruit and train 20 volunteers with the footage set to go on display. Working with the North West Film Archive, volunteers will receive specialist training including in archive handling, digitisation, cataloguing, metadata and preservation. The company have urged anyone who has been involved in any films over the past 25 years to contact them so they can be reunited with their footage. candidates.evidence_text: Homeless charity says 'no change' in Manchester rough sleeping despite PM's pledge - BBC News Image caption, Dave Evans co-founded a homeless charity to help support those in need By Anna Jameson and Lauren Hirst , North West Published 26 November 2026 A homeless charity's co-founder has said he fears Andy Burnham will not be able to meet his pledge to end rough sleeping as the number of those sleeping on the streets in Manchester continues to rise. When he entered Downing Street in the summer, the prime minister pledged to provide a route out of rough sleeping by Christmas through a £442m package of emergency accommodation and practical support over three years. A further £432m was added to the scheme in October. However, with just weeks to go until Christmas, Dave Evans, from the Two Brews charity, said he believed rough sleeping had "gone up dramatically" as he witnessed the daily struggle of those on the streets. When Burnham was first elected as the Mayor of Greater Manchester in May 2017, he made the same pledge to end the need for rough sleeping across all 10 boroughs. He made a great start with the number of rough sleepers in Greater Manchester reducing during the pandemic to 89 in 2021 from 268 in 2017. But over the last five years, numbers have been creeping up. The latest annual rough sleeping snapshot, where local authorities in England provide a figure on any one night in Autumn, shows Greater Manchester has 197 rough sleepers, 43 more than in 2024. The figures for 2026 are expected early next year. 'Big increase' Jordan Parker, from Two Brews, said he and Evans had started the charity six years ago. "We took out 40 meals a night, now we're taking out a hundred meals a night so we've seen a big increase and we're not seeing any sort of things changing." While the figures from the annual snapshot were still lower than what they were in 2017, Parker said he was unsure it reflected an accurate picture. "That's what we're told," he said "As far as I'm aware they do a certain route around the city centre and there's a lot of people hiding down backstreets, hiding behind bins. "I don't think they get it counted." Two Brews launched in 2020, three months into the coronavirus pandemic. The charity has been feeding Manchester's homeless community every night since then. "What we're seeing at the moment, there's no change as we're only five weeks away from Christmas," said Dave. "Hopefully in the next five weeks we can see a change but at the moment we're seeing no change." The Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government said: "The prime minister has pledged to end rough sleeping, backed by £874m of new funding to offer a route off the street to everyone sleeping rough by Christmas and ensure support continues beyond this winter." Image caption, John Herstell says Burnham had been a "breath of fresh air for Manchester" The current Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig has written to businesses, landlords and property owners to help find 100 beds for people rough sleeping in the area. John Herstell, from Supporting People in Need in Ardwick, said he was "hopeful" over Burnham's pledge. "If anyone is going to do it, he's going to do it," said John, after describing him as a "breath of fresh air for Manchester" Twenty-three-year-old Nasir is among those sleeping on the streets, after coming to the UK in 2015 and going through Manchester's education system. "I have been homeless for six or seven weeks," he said. "I need somewhere to wake up, to do something with my life." Image caption, Nasir says he needs more support after sleeping rough for the past few weeks A Manchester City Council spokesperson said there was "a huge amount of work going on to help prevent people from becoming homeless in the first place, and to help anyone who ends up on the streets to get off them as quickly as possible and ultimately into settled accommodation". "Our rough sleeper team are regularly out engaging with anyone sleeping rough to help them access support. "We also work with a wide range of charities and voluntary sector organisations through the Manchester Homelessness Partnership to help ensure there's support for a wide range of circumstances and needs." candidates.lead: Lorna Young was subjected to a "Kafkaesque" investigation into her social media posts, a judge rules
candidates.evidence_text: An equality and diversity manager was unfairly sacked after a "Kafkaesque" investigation into her liking or commenting on posts critical of transgender ideology, a judge has ruled Lorna Young was dismissed by Manchester City Council in 2024 after a staff member found an account on X linked to her which included posts critical of trans themes and a comment that a non-binary vicar had been guided by "the devil" An employment tribunal heard that Young, a devout Catholic in her 50s, was at the time under investigation following complaints from some of her team after she had asked them to research gender recognition perspectives while producing a report for the authority The investigation into those initial complaints expanded when one of the employees discovered another account Young ran under the name Galway Girl, and the council eventually dismissed her on the basis of that account's activity However, in a 90-page ruling , external , Employment Judge Dunlop concluded Young had been the subject of an "amorphous and vague" investigation that failed to properly explain to her the complaints she was facing She also said Young's gender-critical views were protected beliefs, but the council and some of its employees appeared to have taken the view her beliefs were intolerable
candidates.what_happened: Gender-critical equality officer unfairly sacked by council
candidates.source_evidence: Lorna Young was dismissed by Manchester City Council in 2024 after a staff member found an account on X linked to her which included posts critical of trans themes and a comment that a non-binary vicar had been guided by "the devil" An employment tribunal heard that Young, a devout Catholic in her 50s, was at the time under investigation following complaints from some of her team after she had asked them to research gender recognition perspectives while producing a report for the authority The investigation into those initial complaints expanded when one of the employees discovered another account Young ran under the name Galway Girl, and the council eventually dismissed her on the basis of that account's activity However, in a 90-page ruling , Employment Judge Dunlop concluded Young had been the subject of an "amorphous and vague" investigation that failed to properly explain to her the complaints she was facing She also said Young's gender-critical views were protected beliefs, but the council and some of its employees appeared to have taken the view her beliefs were intolerable The judge said Young suffered from a disability affecting her sight, but also became physically and mentally very ill during the lengthy investigation, and at one point made an attempt on her own life

candidates.lead: The woman told a court suggestions she was 'pretending to be asleep' were 'absolute rubbish'
candidates.evidence_text: Warning: This article contains distressing content A woman who had been drugged and raped by her husband for 20 years asked police: "Is it my fault he's done this?", a court heard The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's right to anonymity, has admitted a litany of offences against her - including rape, administering a substance with intent and inviting 13 other men to join the abuse Nine of those men have pleaded not guilty to sexual offences against her and are standing trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Giving evidence in court for the first time, the woman also said claims she had been "pretending to be asleep" during the abuse were a "load of rubbish" The victim, in her 60s, was formally interviewed by Greater Manchester Police on 7 November last year, around two weeks after officers had arrived at her family home to arrest her husband
candidates.what_happened: Wife drugged and raped by husband asked police if she was to blame, court hears
candidates.source_evidence: A woman who had been drugged and raped by her husband for 20 years asked police: "Is it my fault he's done this?", a court heard The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's right to anonymity, has admitted a litany of offences against her - including rape, administering a substance with intent and inviting 13 other men to join the abuse Nine of those men have pleaded not guilty to sexual offences against her and are standing trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Giving evidence in court for the first time, the woman also said claims she had been "pretending to be asleep" during the abuse were a "load of rubbish" The victim, in her 60s, was formally interviewed by Greater Manchester Police on 7 November last year, around two weeks after officers had arrived at her family home to arrest her husband In the interview, played to the jury, she told Det Con Anouska Barker: "I had no knowledge of what you told me had happened and I still can't believe it's true, and I think you have made a mistake."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A three-year-old boy died after choking at a Greater Manchester nursery earlier this month, an inquest heard Thiago Wall died on 5 November after becoming critically ill at Cosy Toes Nursery, in Middleton, on 2 November An inquest at Rochdale Coroner's Court heard on Wednesday that Thiago had choked on a bowl of food and died three days later at the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital. A CT scan later confirmed the toddler had suffered a brain injury The nursery - and three other nurseries owned by Cosy Toes LTD - remain closed The inquest heard the toddler had a hypoxic brain injury, which can be a result of decreased oxygen supply to the brain An investigation by Greater Manchester Police continues

candidates.evidence_text: A nuclear test veteran who developed cancer and lost his four-month-old son, has said hearing an independent panel will look into Britain's atomic programme was "a magical moment" John Morris, from Rochdale, was sent to Christmas Island in the 1950s to work on the UK's growing nuclear programme - and now believes the loss of his son was due to radiation exposure picked up on the island It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced an investigation into the lasting health impacts of testing exercises in the 1950s and 60s Morris, who alongside fellow veterans have long campaigned for an investigation, said this announcement feels different "without a shadow of a doubt" "He [Burnham] has delivered something that has taken more than 70 years to come to fruition, I can't thank you enough," Morris told BBC North West Tonight Morris said he was 18 when he was sent to Christmas Island, in the Pacific Ocean, to work as a laundry operator on a British nuclear site

candidates.evidence_text: A homeless charity's co-founder has said he fears Andy Burnham will not be able to meet his pledge to end rough sleeping as the number of those sleeping on the streets in Manchester continues to rise When he entered Downing Street in the summer, the prime minister pledged to provide a route out of rough sleeping by Christmas through a £442m package of emergency accommodation and practical support over three years A further £432m was added to the scheme in October However, with just weeks to go until Christmas, Dave Evans, from the Two Brews charity, said he believed rough sleeping had "gone up dramatically" as he witnessed the daily struggle of those on the streets When Burnham was first elected as the Mayor of Greater Manchester in May 2017, he made the same pledge to end the need for rough sleeping across all 10 boroughs He made a great start with the number of rough sleepers in Greater Manchester reducing during the pandemic to 89 in 2021 from 268 in 2017

candidates.evidence_text: An equality and diversity manager was unfairly sacked after a "Kafkaesque" investigation into her liking or commenting on posts critical of transgender ideology, a judge has ruled Lorna Young was dismissed by Manchester City Council in 2024 after a staff member found an account on X linked to her which included posts critical of trans themes and a comment that a non-binary vicar had been guided by "the devil" An employment tribunal heard that Young, a devout Catholic in her 50s, was at the time under investigation following complaints from some of her team after she had asked them to research gender recognition perspectives while producing a report for the authority The investigation into those initial complaints expanded when one of the employees discovered another account Young ran under the name Galway Girl, and the council eventually dismissed her on the basis of that account's activity However, in a 90-page ruling , external , Employment Judge Dunlop concluded Young had been the subject of an "amorphous and vague" investigation that failed to properly explain to her the complaints she was facing She also said Young's gender-critical views were protected beliefs, but the council and some of its employees appeared to have taken the view her beliefs were intolerable

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester weather Met Office issues 10-hour ice warning as Greater Manchester temperatures plummet There is the chance freezing rain could turn to snow in some areas Add to preferred sources Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 21:36, 26 Nov 2 A ten-hour warning for ice has been issued for parts of Greater Manchester as temperatures plummet across the region. According to the Met Office, stretches of roads, pavements and cycle paths could become impassable, and public transport could be delayed The yellow alert comes into force at 4am on Friday morning (November 27), and will last until 2pm in the afternoon. It covers eastern parts of Greater Manchester, and stretches north as far as the A69 heading to the east coast from Carlisle The ice will be formed by a patch of freezing rain travelling eastwards. The Met say there may be a 'slight chance' that public transport services are delayed or cancelled, with some road closures and longer journey times a possibility Motorists and pedestrians will be at risk thanks to a chance of icy roads. Those on foot have been advised there may be a 'small chance' of injuries from slips and falls on icy surfaces The regions covered by the yellow weather warning include, Derbyshire, Durham, Northumberland, Cheshire East, Cumbria, Greater Manchester. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Council backs new rules on which flags can be flown over Bolton town hall The Reform propsoed motion said that council-owned civic buildings should reflect ‘what brings Bolton residents together rather than issues which may divide opinion’ Add Bolton council has backed new guidance for flying flags at the borough’s civic buildings. A majority of councillors backed a motion from Reform UK leader Trevor Jones titled ‘putting Bolton and Britain first on civic buildings’ The motion said council-owned civic buildings should reflect ‘what brings Bolton residents together rather than issues which may divide opinion’ It requested the town hall should remain politically impartial and should not be seen to ‘endorse particular political causes, campaigns, movements, foreign governments or international disputes and that decisions regarding the display of flags’ It added that the policy on flags on civic buildings should be ‘taken consistently regardless of the popularity, political support or public profile of a particular cause, campaign or issue’ Coun Jones said: “Council buildings belong to the people of Bolton, appeared for by the people of Bolton, and should represent the people of Bolton

candidates.evidence_text: Salford The ‘gift’ a Salford councillor is giving his residents in the run up to Christmas It will save residents around £3.50 - but it's a commitment to local businesses. Add to preferred sources Comments News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter A Salford councillor is giving locals a ‘gift’ in the run up to Christmas . Residents in Eccles will benefit from free parking at the area’s seven car parks on the three Saturdays leading up to the festive period The move will save residents a ‘small amount of money in the run up to the most expensive time of year’, according to local councillor Mike McCusker. The scheme applies to seven council-run car parks in Eccles, Monton, and Swinton , which are on Hankinson Way, John William Street The scheme is also geared at supporting local businesses, with the hope that locals might make use of their highstreet offers instead of ordering all their Christmas shopping online Councillor McCusker, who represents Eccles, said: “We’ve got a gift for you in the seven car parks that Salford City Council runs. You can get free parking on the free Saturdays leading up to Christmas. It will help you save a small amount of money at this expensive time of year. He added: “We’re delighted to bring back free festive parking this Christmas, helping residents save a little extra money at what can be an expensive time of year, while giving our local businesses a welcome boost

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Council backs new rules on which flags can be flown over Bolton town hall The Reform propsoed motion said that council-owned civic buildings should reflect ‘what brings Bolton residents together rather than issues which may divide opinion’ Add Bolton council has backed new guidance for flying flags at the borough’s civic buildings. A majority of councillors backed a motion from Reform UK leader Trevor Jones titled ‘putting Bolton and Britain first on civic buildings’ The motion said council-owned civic buildings should reflect ‘what brings Bolton residents together rather than issues which may divide opinion’ It requested the town hall should remain politically impartial and should not be seen to ‘endorse particular political causes, campaigns, movements, foreign governments or international disputes and that decisions regarding the display of flags’ It added that the policy on flags on civic buildings should be ‘taken consistently regardless of the popularity, political support or public profile of a particular cause, campaign or issue’ Coun Jones said: “Council buildings belong to the people of Bolton, appeared for by the people of Bolton, and should represent the people of Bolton

Officers from GMP's Serious Organised Crime Group worked with Canadian officials to pull off the dramatic bust on Wednesday evening (November 25) Greater Manchester Police says it was alerted about plans to smuggle 590kg of cannabis by Canadian authorities. It was concealed among a large shipment headed to the UK According to police, drug dealers had created sophisticated compartments inside a container with the hopes that the illegal drugs would go undetected. The container, which arrived at the docks in Liverpool, was closely followed as it was delivered by an HGV to an address in Heywo Officers covertly watched as several people interacted with the container, a spokesperson for GMP said. Members of the force observed as heavy lifting equipment, including a telescopic handler, was used to remove the cargo Officers also witnessed several people take photographs and videos inside the container, with some engaged in lengthy phone calls during the unloading process

candidates.evidence_text: Courts 'I'm here to tell the truth': Husband who drugged and raped wife for more than 20 years weeps as he gives evidence for first time The man took to the witness box to be questioned by prosecutors. Nine defendants are on trial in the case. Top row Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 19:21, 26 Nov 2026 Updated 19:38, 26 Nov 2026 Perhaps it was the moment that the enormity of his crimes finally hit him. As he made his way into the witness box, where his wife had calmly answered questions for 45 minut Why, after initially pleading not guilty, then changing his plea, was this the moment he wanted to speak out? “So the court knows the truth of what happened to my wife, so my wife knows and I’m here to tell the truth and give my account of what actually happened," he said In a navy suit and tie, the husband, a man in his 60s from Stockport, faced questioning from prosecutors all day on Thursday (November 26). "For you, why is it important that you are here in this trial?"," Louise Oakley KC, the lead prosecutor, asked It was then that he broke down for the first time, appearing visibly emotional. He apologised, as he took a few seconds to compose himself. "Take your time," Judge Maurice Greene told him. The husband said: "So I can tell the truth of what happened to [his wife]." Then, the prosecutor laid out charge after charge which he has admitted, 60 crimes committed over a 20 year period until his arrest in October last year. They included conspiracy to rape, rape, assault by penetration, and conspiracy to administer a substance with intent

candidates.evidence_text: Bee Network Greater Manchester passengers to be asked how Bee Network buses can be better A disability campaigner said 'even when most of a journey is accessible, one barrier along the way can make the whole journey difficult' Add to preferred sources Bus users across Greater Manchester are being asked how the Bee Network services can be more accessible. A consultation on the city-region’s first Bus Network Accessibility Plan starts next week which hopes to get a wide range of feedback how bus travel can be improved The draft plan states that several barriers to accessibility remain on the network These include access to bus stops, availability of passenger information, ease of boarding, availability of assistance and the consistency of facilities at Greater Manchester’s interchanges Recent changes to improve accessibility have included audio-visual announcements and next-stop screens on buses, hearing loops, high-contrast handrails and anti-slip flooring Newer buses also include two dedicated wheelchair spaces and room for an assistance dog close to its owner

I can be my version of me, not his' Selena is one of more than 1,800 people in Greater Manchester who secured a Domestic Abuse Protection Order (DAPO) in the last two y ‘It got me home’, Selena tells me. She is one of more than 1,800 people in Greater Manchester who have had a Domestic Abuse Protection Order (DAPO) issued over the last two years Hers is the result of an abusive relationship she says started when she was 16. The court-issued order puts legally binding restrictions on her now ex-boyfriend, including blocking him from contacting her or entering anywhere he believes she could be The 23-year-old, who we are calling Selena, said the relationship had turned her into ‘his version’ of her. She credits the DAPO as a huge part of the reason she was able to reclaim her life and her home for herself and her young daughter Selena said her ex breached her DAPO twice. He pleaded guilty and is currently awaiting sentencing for that second breach She told the Manchester Evening News the relationship started in 2019 when she was 16, ‘very young’, ‘naïve’ and ‘impressionable’. When the country went into lockdown as a result of Covid-19 , he moved in with her family

A tribunal ruled the town hall unfairly dismissed and unlawfully discriminated against disabled employee Lorna Young after colleagues raised objections over her gender-critic Ms Young, who worked for the council for nearly 19 years as an equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI) manager, managed long-term health conditions throughout her employment, including a serious eye condition that required multiple operations Despite carrying out her responsibilities 'professionally and scrupulously' - including on matters relating to trans issues - she faced a 'slew' of complaints from colleagues about her perceived beliefs, an employment tribunal heard. Those included objections to her social media The complaints centred on Ms Young liking posts on Twitter , now known as X, which either contained gender-critical content or were shared by prominent advocates of those views, including JK Rowling and Julie Bindel. A judge characterised the complaints as 'a campaign against an The council put Ms Young under disciplinary proceedings described as 'Kafkaesque' and 'particularly callous' by the judge, who concluded the town hall's conduct was 'egregiously unfair'

The first report of theft was made on October 31 when the same Morrisons store on Atherton Road was targeted Following the incident, eight more robberies are believed to have taken place with the latest one reported at around 6.55am today. GMP say a man wearing dark clothing and face covering entered the store, jumped over the counter and threatened staff with a metal bar A CSI van has been pictured outside the store after the altercation. It is believed that around £10,000 in cash has been stolen from all nine robberies conducted in the Wigan area Detectives have been carrying out extensive enquiries, including reviewing CCTV footage, gathering intelligence and speaking with local businesses and members of the community

Since October 31, new government reforms on how planning applications are approved or denied have been in place To comply with the law, the council was required to change its scheme of delegation for planning matters, otherwise the planning committee would not be allowed to sit and any decisions made after October 31 would be unlawful Under the changes, more applications will be decided by planning officers rather than by a planning committee of elected members The Labour government has said this would make planning applications quicker, more efficient and reduce the number of decisions overturned on appeal. Larger and more contentious applications would still need approval from planning committees Opposition councillors argued that the changes should be rejected. Speaking at a full council meeting, Reform UK leader Coun Paul Watson, said: “We are not simply elected to rubber stamp the wishes of national government

candidates.evidence_text: East Manchester Major road near Etihad Stadium to reopen eight MONTHS after giant hole appeared The busy stretch of road in east Manchester has been shut off for eight months after a historic mineshaft caused the road to collapse Add to preferred sour A stretch of one of Manchester’s busiest roads is to reopen after eight months of work fixing a giant hole. The northbound section of Alan Turing Way, in Beswick close to the Etihad Stadium , was shut off in March after a suspected sinkhole was discovered For months the council wasn’t entirely sure what had caused the stretch of road to collapse. But in September, engineers discovered it was a 50m-deep mineshaft under the road that triggered the 3m-wide crater There is a long history of mining and colliers throughout east Manchester, but this mineshaft wasn’t recorded on historic maps and took workers by surprise. Further investigations revealed the extent of the cavity and scale of repairs required In order to stabilise the shaft, contractors filled it with 120 tonnes of concrete grout before putting a ‘reinforced concrete slab’ over the top. Concrete has also been used to 'backfill' the original excavation with utilities pipes, and the road surface, then being restored In an update, Manchester City Council said the 'unprecedented' and 'highly complex' works were 'reaching their conclusion' and that the road would reopen on Saturday, November 28. It is expected to be clear by mid-morning

It covers eastern parts of Greater Manchester, and stretches north as far as the A69 heading to the east coast from Carlisle The ice will be formed by a patch of freezing rain travelling eastwards. Add to preferred sources Comments News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter A Salford councillor is giving locals a ‘gift’ in the run up to Christmas . Residents in Eccles will benefit from free parking at the area’s seven car parks on the three Saturdays leading up to the festive period The move will save residents a ‘small amount of money in the run up to the most expensive time of year’, according to local councillor Mike McCusker. Officers from GMP's Serious Organised Crime Group worked with Canadian officials to pull off the dramatic bust on Wednesday evening (November 25) Greater Manchester Police says it was alerted about plans to smuggle 590kg of cannabis by Canadian authorities. A consultation on the city-region’s first Bus Network Accessibility Plan starts next week which hopes to get a wide range of feedback how bus travel can be improved The draft plan states that several barriers to accessibility remain on the network These include access to bus stops, availability of passenger information, ease of boarding, availability of assistance and the consistency of facilities at Greater Manchester’s interchanges Recent changes to improve accessibility have included audio-visual announcements and next-stop screens on buses, hearing loops, high-contrast handrails and anti-slip flooring Newer buses also include two dedicated wheelchair spaces and room for an assistance dog close to its owner

candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police 'My life was consumed by him... now I can finally be me. I can be my version of me, not his' Selena is one of more than 1,800 people in Greater Manchester who secured a Domestic Abuse Protection Order (DAPO) in the last two y ‘It got me home’, Selena tells me. She is one of more than 1,800 people in Greater Manchester who have had a Domestic Abuse Protection Order (DAPO) issued over the last two years Hers is the result of an abusive relationship she says started when she was 16. The court-issued order puts legally binding restrictions on her now ex-boyfriend, including blocking him from contacting her or entering anywhere he believes she could be The 23-year-old, who we are calling Selena, said the relationship had turned her into ‘his version’ of her. She credits the DAPO as a huge part of the reason she was able to reclaim her life and her home for herself and her young daughter Selena said her ex breached her DAPO twice. He pleaded guilty and is currently awaiting sentencing for that second breach She told the Manchester Evening News the relationship started in 2019 when she was 16, ‘very young’, ‘naïve’ and ‘impressionable’. When the country went into lockdown as a result of Covid-19 , he moved in with her family

Since October 31, new government reforms on how planning applications are approved or denied have been in place To comply with the law, the council was required to change its scheme of delegation for planning matters, otherwise the planning committee would not be allowed to sit and any decisions made after October 31 would be unlawful Under the changes, more applications will be decided by planning officers rather than by a planning committee of elected members The Labour government has said this would make planning applications quicker, more efficient and reduce the number of decisions overturned on appeal. Larger and more contentious applications would still need approval from planning committees Opposition councillors argued that the changes should be rejected. Speaking at a full council meeting, Reform UK leader Coun Paul Watson, said: “We are not simply elected to rubber stamp the wishes of national government

candidates.evidence_text: East Manchester Major road near Etihad Stadium to reopen eight MONTHS after giant hole appeared The busy stretch of road in east Manchester has been shut off for eight months after a historic mineshaft caused the road to collapse Add to preferred sour A stretch of one of Manchester’s busiest roads is to reopen after eight months of work fixing a giant hole. The northbound section of Alan Turing Way, in Beswick close to the Etihad Stadium , was shut off in March after a suspected sinkhole was discovered For months the council wasn’t entirely sure what had caused the stretch of road to collapse. But in September, engineers discovered it was a 50m-deep mineshaft under the road that triggered the 3m-wide crater There is a long history of mining and colliers throughout east Manchester, but this mineshaft wasn’t recorded on historic maps and took workers by surprise. Further investigations revealed the extent of the cavity and scale of repairs required In order to stabilise the shaft, contractors filled it with 120 tonnes of concrete grout before putting a ‘reinforced concrete slab’ over the top. Concrete has also been used to 'backfill' the original excavation with utilities pipes, and the road surface, then being restored In an update, Manchester City Council said the 'unprecedented' and 'highly complex' works were 'reaching their conclusion' and that the road would reopen on Saturday, November 28. It is expected to be clear by mid-morning

candidates.evidence_text: Courts They'd been friends since high school, but one tragic decision would change their lives forever 'This was a grave and catastrophic error in judgement from a young and inexperienced driver' Abdul Wahab, 23 (Image: GMP) Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 05:43, 26 Nov 2026 Updated 06:14, 26 Nov 2026 Abdul Wahab had not been drinking or taking drugs on the evening of January 1, 2024. He had simply been eating and talking at the Rochdale home of his friend Saeed B It was Abdullah Mazhar, another friend, asking if he could join them. The trio had been best mates since high school, and then 20-year-old Wahab thought little of the ten minute journey in Saeed's grey Seat Ibiza It was dark, the rain was heavy. But a court would later hear how Wahab wasn't somebody anyone would describe as a 'thrill-seeker'. Yet a decision he was about to make would have tragic consequences, and change the trajectory of the three friends' lives forever In front of a busy public gallery packed with the victims' and defendant's friends and family at Minshull Street Crown Court yesterday (November 25)., prosecutor Maria Brannan described the trio's close friendship Initially, it was agreed that Saeed would drive to Mr Mazhar’s home on West Street to pick him up

candidates.evidence_text: Thursday 19 November 2026 at 3:49pm Four children died after petrol bombs were thrown into their home in Salford in 2017, their mother died two years later after suffering severe burns Credit: ITV News The family of a mother murdered with her four youngest children say failings b Single mother-of-six Michelle Pearson had called police multiple times, told family social workers she wanted to move and asked to be rehoused before suffering fatal injuries in the firebombing of her home on Jackson Street, Walkden, in the early hours of 11 December 2017 The 37-year-old's four youngest children, Demi Pearson, 14, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, were also murdered as flames engulfed the house Michelle Pearson (left) , Demi (middle), Brandon (right), Lacie and Lia Credit: Family pictures Final submissions from the lawyers for the family, police, local council and others were heard on Wednesday following a seven-week inquest hearing at Bolton Coroner’s Court The hearing was told the only possible conclusion by the coroner is the family were unlawfully killed But lawyers for the parties differ on whether other agencies, especially the police, could be found to have probably contributed to or caused the deaths

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

candidates.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email Here’s a first look inside Altrincham’s newest coffee shop, 200 Degrees, which officially opens its doors at 9am this Saturday, 28 November The Nottingham-founded speciality coffee company has taken the last of the three retail units created from the former Wilko and Poundland building on George Street - we exclusively revealed in October - completing the redevelopment alongside Oliver Bonas and FatFace The Altrincham shop is the company’s 28th in the UK and its third in Greater Manchester, joining existing branches on Mosley Street in Manchester city centre and Wilmslow Road in Didsbury Founded in 2012, 200 Degrees has built its reputation around speciality coffee, roasting its own beans and placing an emphasis on the craft of coffee-making Customers can expect a range of espresso-based drinks and filter coffees alongside a selection of food and sweet treats, with the company’s own coffee beans also available to buy and enjoy at home There will be giveaways to mark Saturday’s official opening, including the chance to win a Sage coffee machine

candidates.evidence_text: Lorna Young was dismissed by Manchester City Council in 2024 after a staff member found an account on X linked to her which included posts critical of trans themes and a comment that a non-binary vicar had been guided by "the devil" An employment tribunal heard that Young, a devout Catholic in her 50s, was at the time under investigation following complaints from some of her team after she had asked them to research gender recognition perspectives while producing a report for the authority The investigation into those initial complaints expanded when one of the employees discovered another account Young ran under the name Galway Girl, and the council eventually dismissed her on the basis of that account's activity However, in a 90-page ruling , Employment Judge Dunlop concluded Young had been the subject of an "amorphous and vague" investigation that failed to properly explain to her the complaints she was facing She also said Young's gender-critical views were protected beliefs, but the council and some of its employees appeared to have taken the view her beliefs were intolerable The judge said Young suffered from a disability affecting her sight, but also became physically and mentally very ill during the lengthy investigation, and at one point made an attempt on her own life

candidates.evidence_text: A woman who had been drugged and raped by her husband for 20 years asked police: "Is it my fault he's done this?", a court heard The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's right to anonymity, has admitted a litany of offences against her - including rape, administering a substance with intent and inviting 13 other men to join the abuse Nine of those men have pleaded not guilty to sexual offences against her and are standing trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Giving evidence in court for the first time, the woman also said claims she had been "pretending to be asleep" during the abuse were a "load of rubbish" The victim, in her 60s, was formally interviewed by Greater Manchester Police on 7 November last year, around two weeks after officers had arrived at her family home to arrest her husband In the interview, played to the jury, she told Det Con Anouska Barker: "I had no knowledge of what you told me had happened and I still can't believe it's true, and I think you have made a mistake."

candidates.lead: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund
candidates.evidence_text: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund The funding forms part of an £18million government programme to create or refurbish playgrounds in England's areas of greatest need over the next two years The government selected Failsworth to receive a share of the fund, with three play areas identified as eligible for investment through the programme for 66 local authorities Funding will be used to improve playground facilities and support community-led design and engagement activities, giving residents the opportunity to help shape the future of these spaces The three eligible sites are Higher Memorial Park which will receive £160,000, Daisy Nook Country Park which will receive £60,000 and Lower Memorial Park which has been allocated £50,000 A larger share will go to Higher Memorial Park because this has received significantly less external investment than the other locations in recent years

candidates.lead: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026
candidates.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026 The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications Residents will be asked the following question “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area

candidates.evidence_text: More than 100,000 visitors flocked to Bolton town centre for this year’s Put Big Light On Festival, making the four-day event one of the borough’s most successful cultural celebrations to date From Thursday 19 to Sunday 22 November, residents and visitors enjoyed an unforgettable programme of illuminated art installations, interactive experiences, street theatre, live performances, and larger-than-life creations across the town centre At the heart of the festival was the stunning Loom of Light installation in Victoria Square, inspired by Bolton’s rich textile heritage, while thousands of visitors explored a diverse programme featuring internationally acclaimed artworks including Helios, DUNDU, Event Horizon, K The festival, delivered by Bolton Council in partnership with Things That Go On Things, also provided a significant boost to local businesses, with visitors spending time in the town’s shops, cafes, restaurants, and cultural venues throughout the event Bolton Council’s Executive Cabinet Member for Culture, Cllr Debbie Newall, said To welcome more than 100,000 visitors to our town centre is a fantastic achievement and a huge boost for our local businesses

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

candidates.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

Loungers to open Fosforo Lounge in Stretford on Saturday 28th November. By. About Manchester - . . November 9, 2026 0 . . . . . . Facebook. . Twitter. . Google+. . Pinterest. . WhatsApp. . . . . . Cadno Lounge, Neath . Loungers, the West Country‑based café‑bar group, will open Fosforo Lounge, King Street in Stretford on Saturday 28th November 2026, creating around 30 new jobs for local people.. . Fosforo Lounge will be open all day, every day, serving breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner and drinks, with dedicated kids’, gluten‑free and vegan menus. . The site on King Street has been transformed by the Loungers design team into a warm, eclectic ‘home from home’ – their signature style. Fosforo translates to matchstick and is a nod to Manchester-based painter LS Lowry’s ‘matchstick men’ style.. . Fosforo Lounge’s all‑day menu will cater for every taste, from hearty comfort food to healthier choices and indulgent treats. Families are a major focus, with games, books, colouring materials, high chairs and baby‑changing facilities available for Little Loungers.. . With community at its heart, Fosforo Lounge will offer a welcoming space for regular meet‑ups, business catch‑ups, book clubs, knitting groups, parent‑and‑baby sessions, creative workshops and more. Local groups looking for a friendly, flexible venue will be encouraged to get in touch.. . Vix Connolly, General Manager, Fosforo Lounge said: “We’re so looking forward to welcoming everyone to Fosforo Lounge on the 28th November. Becoming a genuine part of the community is incredibly important to us, and we can’t wait to meet our neighbours and get involved locally.. . “If you’re looking for a friendly, flexible space for events or group meet‑ups, pop in once we’re open – we’d love to chat and see how we can help.”. . . . . . . Facilities Wheelchair Accessible Toilets All Outdoor Seating Available Dog Friendly Free Entry Markets in Manchester , North West , Greater Manchester , The North Browse from 75 stallholders at Quayside Media City Makers Market, where you can meet local producers, browse the independent stalls, sample delicious street food and enjoy live music and entertaining performances as you wander through town. All of the independent traders showcasing here produce high quality, handmade, artisan goods. The Makers Market pride themselves on having a wide range of truly unique stallholders, offering delicious treats, amazing art and craft and so much more. Whether you’re looking for an ideal gift, a treat for yourself, or just topping up your weekly shopping, this market is a great place to spend time at the weekend. candidates.evidence_text: Clint Boon spinning records on Greek Street on a Saturday afternoon, and it won’t cost you a penny. Stopford Park is throwing a free party to launch Bosden, the first of its new apartment buildings, just up from the Town Hall Clint Boon needs very little introduction round these parts. The Inspiral Carpets man was right in the middle of Madchester and he’s still at it, touring and recently publishing his book, The Manchester Chronicles . He’ll be sharing the decks with DJ, presenter and podcaster Matt There’ll be a talk from John Barratt, co-founder of the Stockport Music Story with his wife Rosemary. John founded the record label Facsimile Liaisons which took him to Strawberry Studios, he’s worked with Easterhouse and Syncopation, and also signed The Family Foundation, Ultrac There will be a pop-up from I Knead Pizza, and it’s also the first chance to have a nosey round the show apartment at Bosden with the remaining apartments going on the market the same day. If you’re tempted to have a look round you can register your interest here Make a weekend of it: Foodie Friday is on across the Market Place and Great Underbank the night before, from 6pm

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester brand specialist delivers pro bono package for mid-career redundancy-focused social enterprise - Prolific North Skip to content News Telefónica Tech recommits to Scotland News “Food, friendship and fearless comedy” – BBC commissions digital-first format Agency Authentic travel brief for Aberfield Manchester brand specialist delivers pro bono package for mid-career redundancy-focused social enterprise Agency by Chris Newbould November 26, 2026 Manchester-based brand consultancy Greater Else has delivered a comprehensive branding and digital package pro bono to support the launch of a career transition programme helping experienced professionals rebuild their careers after redundancy, with plans for a national rollout following a successful London pilot. Greater Else, which also has an office in Leeds, has partnered with social enterprise Avenir Pathways to support the launch of Future Reset, a programme designed to help mid-career professionals regain their confidence, develop new skills and return to employment after redundancy. The consultancy has delivered the work entirely pro bono, creating Avenir Pathways’ brand identity, messaging and tone of voice, website, 2026 Social Impact Report and supporting launch materials, including event branding and promotional collateral. READ MORE: Leeds agency goes viral after Elon Musk shares latest Tesla collaboration clip The programme launched in London yesterday (25 November), alongside Avenir Pathways’ debut Social Impact Report, following a pilot in July that saw 44% of participants in paid employment three months after completing the programme, including those returning to full-time roles and freelance or contract work. Building on the pilot’s early results, Avenir Pathways is now planning to take Future Reset beyond London and expand its reach nationally, with further funding and partnerships being sought to support the next stage. Greater Else is backing those ambitions and would welcome the programme’s expansion into Greater Manchester and the wider North West, where the consultancy says redundancies and a challenging recruitment market are affecting experienced professionals across the creative, marketing and digital industries. Future Reset was developed following research with more than 50 professionals affected by redundancy. It aims to address a gap in career support for experienced employees who are neither at the beginning of their careers nor in senior executive positions. Rather than focusing solely on CV writing and job applications, the programme takes participants through three stages, Reset, Re-equip and Reboot, helping them rebuild confidence, identify transferable skills, develop their understanding of AI and digital tools, and create a practical plan for returning to work. Geoff Bretherick, creative director at Greater Else, said: “Redundancy is difficult at any stage of your career, but there’s something particularly unsettling about being made redundant after spending 15 or 20 years building your experience, skills and professional reputation. “We’ve seen incredibly talented people across the creative, marketing and digital industries struggling to find their next opportunity, and it’s an issue that feels very close to home for us. “That’s why we wanted to get behind Avenir Pathways. We could see the difference this programme was trying to make, and we had the expertise to help them build a strong brand and platform to take it forward. Providing that support pro bono was an easy decision. “The pilot has already shown encouraging results, and the ambition now is to take the programme further. We’d love to see that include Greater Manchester and the wider North West. The challenges facing experienced professionals aren’t exclusive to London, and support like this could make a real difference to people across the North.” Founded by former advertising and marketing professional Dinah Williams, Avenir Pathways is working to address the impact of redundancy on professional confidence, career identity and the ability to navigate an increasingly competitive employment market. Chris Bennett, strategy director at Greater Else, added: “At its heart, this project is about helping people recognise and communicate their value, something we work with businesses on every day. “When experienced professionals are made redundant, the challenge often goes beyond finding another job. candidates.evidence_text: Unbranded Manchester unveils relaunched Film Locations digital scouting platform - Prolific North Skip to content Featured Profile Unbranded Manchester News Telefónica Tech recommits to Scotland News “Food, friendship and fearless comedy” – BBC commissions digital-first format Agency Authentic travel brief for Aberfield Unbranded Manchester unveils relaunched Film Locations digital scouting platform Agency by Chris Newbould November 25, 2026 Digital agency Unbranded Manchester has announced the official relaunch of Film Locations , a fully automated digital platform designed to overhaul how the UK film, television and commercial production industries source, book, and manage filming venues. Launching with an initial portfolio of more than 3,000 properties, studios, and unique venues across the country and beyond, Film Locations removes the traditional bottlenecks of location scouting by providing production agencies and scouts with direct, real-time access to property owners. Film Locations was conceived to address a longstanding frustration in UK production: slow, opaque communication chains and heavy intermediary fees when securing private locations. Unbranded partnered with Film Locations to architect, design, and build the platform from the ground up, engineering a streamlined digital marketplace capable of handling complex search, direct messaging, and end-to-end booking workflows automatically. “Location scouting is one of the most time-sensitive parts of any production, yet the process has historically relied on fragmented directories and endless back-and-forth,” said Hamad Mian , Managing Director at Unbranded Manchester. “When Film Locations brought us their vision, our goal was to build a platform that matched the pace of modern production. By automating the heavy lifting and putting scouts directly in touch with property owners, we’ve created a transparent ecosystem that works for both sides.” READ MORE: Teesside agency celebrates six years with 40% YoY turnover growth and two new hires Key features of the Film Locations platform include: 3,000+ Ready-to-Book Locations: Instant access to an extensive, searchable database spanning private homes, commercial spaces, industrial sites, studios, and architectural landmarks nationwide. Direct Owner Communication: Built-in messaging tools allow scouts and producers to negotiate terms, ask logistical questions, and arrange recces directly with property owners without third-party delays. It also includes messaging via secure WhatsApp integration for all users. End-to-End Automation: Streamlined search filtering, availability management, and booking administration reduce turnaround times of booking recces and locations. “Our mission with Film Locations is simple: make finding and securing extraordinary spaces across the UK effortless,” said Josh Jones, founder of Film Locations. “Unbranded understood that this needed to be a true operational tool for busy production teams and everyday property owners. Launching with 3,000 properties out of the gate shows just how ready the industry is for a direct, modern approach.” Film Locations is now live and open to film scouts, production agencies, and property owners looking to list their spaces across the UK. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . In August, Nothing Gold Can Stay took Robert Frost’s poem about transience as its starting point. Where that show dwelt on things passing, this one is more interested in what lasts The four contributing artists each approach time differently, thinking about how the past and the future shape the way ideas are understood. Anna Clough, a Cumbrian-born artist based at Salford’s Paradise Works, has made walking performances tracing mining landscapes from the Neo Sheffield’s Charlotte Dawson treats everyday objects – souvenirs, collections – as vessels for memory. Olivia England, who graduated from Manchester School of Art alongside Clough, reworks found objects, text and imagery through bookbinding and print, while London-based Elliot Fo Seeing the work from a perspective that isn’t your own is meant to open up conversations about the legacy of ideas, collective memory and what our actions leave behind for people we’ll never meet

The Spaniard admitted to two charges of acting improperly towards the match off On November 8, United faced Villa at Old Trafford , and the contest ended in a draw . candidates.evidence_text: Football Erling Haaland Sulky Man City interviews do not matter but some body language does Rayan Cherki urged his Manchester City teammates to applaud the fans after their 2-2 draw before asking for more energy in an interview Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Simon A lot has been made of Erling Haaland's body language after Manchester City's draw with Napoli. The No.9 was dejected in post-match interviews as he spoke sulkily about the team needing to do better Rayan Cherki struck the same tone, saying that he did not care about scoring goals because he wanted to win and the team did not have enough energy. Enzo Maresca appeared surprised to hear this , needing a few seconds to compose himself in his press conference before diplomatical The sight of Haaland and Cherki unhappy neatly sums up the extent of City's current state. Two of their biggest stars, their goal machine and their most creative player, both failing to hide their frustration after yet another performance that left fans exasperated And yet, put it another way: how should they react? Perhaps it would be more professional to focus on positives and smile through the issues, but the best winners in life tend to be horrible losers If you don't want horrible losers in the team then fine but you are depriving yourself of the players who make the best and biggest winners - ask Rodri and Bernardo Silva. Everyone watching City games can see that there are problems, so Haaland and Cherki reflecting that after on

evidence_packet.summary: Live-концерт MONATIK в Лондоне! 26 февраля 2027 года Indigo at The O2 превратится в место музыки, ритма и свободы, ведь на сцену выйдет вечно танцующий, невероятный исполнитель MONATIK!
evidence_packet.evidence_text: 26 февраля 2027 года Indigo at The O2 превратится в место музыки, ритма и свободы, ведь на сцену выйдет вечно танцующий, невероятный исполнитель MONATIK! Этот концерт — больше, чем просто выступление: это пространство, где публика сливается в едином ритме, проживая что-то настоящ MONATIK отправляется в международный концертный тур, в рамках которого посетит Великобританию! Артист влюбил миллионы слушателей в свою музыку благодаря песням “Кожний раз”, “А що?”, “Сильно”, “Кружить” и многим другим, в каждой из которых ритм занимает центральное место.
